name: Memorial Union Building
use: Student union and New Hampshire's official state war memorial: bookstore, post office, theaters, dining, meeting and function rooms, student organizations
architect: Ronald Gourley (Harvard faculty); builder John A. Volpe Construction

renovations.what: Extensive renovation and addition, including the MUB theaters
Roof replacement: design-services RFQ issued November 2025

facts.text: Built 1957 as student union, conference centre and New Hampshire's official state war memorial; designed by Ronald Gourley and built by John A. Volpe Construction; dedicated October 12, 1957.
Artist and professor John Hatch made the coloured glass window in the war memorial room, the first window in the world to use laminated safety glass decoratively.
Extensively renovated in 1995; the theater addition's debt was still being paid off in 2018.

In 2018 the MUB director said 10,000-12,000 people used it daily and that the roof and largely 1950s electrical system needed replacing within ten years; a full repair was estimated at about $85 million, minimum upkeep about $25 million.
USNH sought design services for a full MUB roof replacement in November 2025.
Now branded the New Hampshire Memorial Union; it houses the bookstore, Cats' Cupboard food pantry, Granite Square Station mail and a games room.

verdict: The state's official war memorial and the student union: stark 1957 brick above a fieldstone wall, heavily used and ageing.
notes: Photo (2013) shows the plaza side: a windowless brick box above a long fieldstone wall, a slim stone tower and a glazed entrance. The massing is stark, and the stone gives it some texture. No interior photos. The old row's list of later projects (balcony 2002, AV 2008, restrooms 2012, south addition) was not verified. Roof project status after the RFQ is unknown. Official name now appears as 'New Hampshire Memorial Union' on Student Life pages; notunh uses 'Memorial Union Building'. A licensed 2018 interior (Flickr, captioned as the bookstore in the MUB) shows a plain corridor with terrazzo floor and glazed shopfront.
judgeNotes: Photo shows a windowless brick box over fieldstone; bookstore corridor ordinary. Exterior down a point from the old run.
